items.question: What exactly is the Process Check?
items.answer: A 60-minute call on Microsoft Teams. We look at one task your team does by hand on a regular basis. I tell you what I'd automate, how big the build would be and what it would cost. Afterwards you get the result in a short written summary.

items.question: Who is it for?
items.answer: Owners, managers and team leads at SMEs where time goes into manual work every week: moving data between systems, putting reports together, entering receipts, chasing customers. It isn't meant for building a new product.

items.question: What do I need to prepare?
items.answer: Work that keeps coming up, or a concrete workflow. A report, an export or a handful of receipts is enough. The hour works best if the person who does that work today joins.

items.question: Which systems does it work with?
items.answer: Anything with an API. We look at what yours offer during the check.

items.question: Do I have to show customer data on the call?
items.answer: No. You can describe the process, or show an example with blacked-out or made-up data. You don't need to send anything beforehand.

items.question: Why isn't it free?
items.answer: Because we spend the hour on your actual work, and you leave with a price you can base a decision on.

items.question: Am I committing to a build?
items.answer: No. You pay for the check and nothing else. If you go ahead later, the fee comes off the build price.

items.question: When is the appointment confirmed?
items.answer: As soon as the payment goes through. Microsoft Bookings then sends you the confirmation with the Teams link.

items.question: Can I reschedule?
items.answer: Yes, free of charge up to 12 hours before. Email or call me. If you don't show up, there's no refund.

items.question: Which language?
items.answer: English, German or Swiss German, whichever you prefer.

bottomCta.title: After an hour you'll know whether it's worth automating.

offer.factsLine: 60 minutes on Microsoft Teams, for CHF 99.

a.hook: Frustrated that someone on your team still retypes data that's already in another system?
a.sub: In the Process Check we look at one of those tasks together. Afterwards you know whether it can be automated and what that would cost.
situation: Timesheets, receipts or orders arrive by email or on paper, and someone types them in.
The monthly report gets rebuilt in Excel from several exports, every time.
There's a ChatGPT subscription. The process itself hasn't changed.
Someone was asked to "look into AI" and doesn't know where to start.

b.hook: Is one of your routine tasks ready to be automated?
b.sub: After an hour you'll know, with a price you can decide on, or take to whoever does. Tell me where your team does manual work every week, and I'll tell you where I'd start.
b.situationTitle: When a task is a good fit
situation: It comes up regularly, every week or every day.
It follows fixed rules, even if there are lots of them.
The data is already digital somewhere, even if that's an email, a PDF or a spreadsheet.

c.hook: Bring one task your team did by hand last week. I'll show you which part of it could run automatically.
c.sub: Ideally a task someone did by hand, from start to finish. By the end of the hour you know what I'd build and roughly what it would cost.
situation: You show me on screen, or just tell me, how the task runs today: where the data comes from, who does what, how often.
I show you where automation can take over and what stays manual.
You get the price range before we hang up.
Afterwards you get it all in a short written summary.
